title: Codex transcript tests: mock node:os homedir and restore CODEX_HOME after each test
answers: How do I test Codex transcript discovery with a fake home directory
Write tests for CODEX_HOME precedence in the Codex integration
Test isolation for process.env in Codex integration jest tests
body:
Convention in libs/typescript/integrations/codex/tests/transcript.test.ts: the file mocks 'node:os' with jest.mock, spreading jest.requireActual and replacing only homedir with jest.fn(), so tests control the legacy home without touching the real ~/.codex.
Each findTranscriptForThread test writes fixture rollouts under mkdtemp directories in tmpdir(), and afterEach restores process.env.CODEX_HOME (delete if it was originally undefined), resets the homedir mock, and removes the temp root.
Keep the three cases covered together: CODEX_HOME takes precedence over the legacy home, unset falls back to ~/.codex, and empty string falls back to ~/.codex.
The source imports homedir from 'node:os', so the mock path must stay 'node:os' or the mock will not apply.
applies: Jest tests for the Codex integration that read environment variables or the home directory.
says: Automated test runs are touching files in the real user home folder.
Codex integration test suites are leaking environment configuration across different tests.
Verify that custom home directory settings properly override default session storage in tests.
Add automated tests ensuring empty directory settings fall back to default user storage.
Clean up temporary fixture folders and reset environment variables after integration tests finish.
